bracket: [Textbook misprint: the printed solution says S and Cl "belong to second period of the periodic table". They belong to the THIRD period — Table 7.1 of this same chapter gives their configurations as \(\mathrm{[Ne]3s^23p^4}\) and \(\mathrm{[Ne]3s^23p^5}\). The argument and the conclusion S < Cl are unaffected, so the solution is preserved as printed.]

[Textbook misprint: the question asks about "pyrosulfurous acid". The chapter names no such acid; the only "pyro" acid of sulfur it teaches is "Di or pyrosulfuric acid, \(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_7}\)" (section 7.8.1), for which the answer is \(+6\). Read literally as pyrosulfurous acid, \(\mathrm{H_2S_2O_5}\), the question would have no correct option at all.]

[Textbook misprint: option B is printed as "IBr > BeF > ICl > ClF > BrCl". "BeF" should read "BrF" — beryllium fluoride is not a halogen compound and cannot appear in an ordering of interhalogens. The option is a distractor either way; the correct order is the one in option C.]

[Textbook misprint: options A and D are printed as \(\mathrm{[I_3]}\) and \(\mathrm{[BrF_4]}\), without their charges. Both species are ANIONS — \(\mathrm{[I_3]^-}\) and \(\mathrm{[BrF_4]^-}\) — and the electron count that fixes their shapes depends on that charge.]

[Textbook misprint: three of the eight equations are defective as printed. (2) gives \(\mathrm{KIO_2}\) where the chapter's own reaction gives \(\mathrm{KIO_3}\) — with \(\mathrm{KIO_2}\) the oxygen cannot balance (3 on the left, 2 on the right). (6) gives \(\mathrm{XeF_4}\) where \(\mathrm{XeOF_4}\) belongs; \(\mathrm{XeF_4} + \mathrm{SiO_2}\) would demand the product \(\mathrm{XeO_2}\), which the chapter never mentions. (7) prints \(6\mathrm{H_2O}\) where the chapter's equation uses \(3\mathrm{H_2O}\); with six, three molecules of water are left over.]

[Textbook misprint: the ionisation enthalpies are printed with the unit "kJ/mol\(^{-1}\)", which reads as kJ\(\cdot\)mol. The unit is kJ mol\(^{-1}\) (equivalently kJ/mol), as Table 7.2 of the chapter is headed. The values themselves are correct.]

[Textbook note (not an error): part (a) sets the reaction of \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\) with \(\mathrm{F_2}\) at 437 K, whereas this chapter's own table of preparations gives \(\mathrm{Cl_2} + \mathrm{F_2} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{ClF}\) at 523 K in a copper vessel. The product is ClF on either reading; only the stated temperature differs from the chapter.]
